title: Helen Keller: The Hand That Found Water
dek: A fever closed sight and sound; touch reopened the world.
mortality_event: At nineteen months, an acute illness left Helen Keller deafblind; at the water pump in 1887, language broke through by touch.
citation_passage: Helen Keller (1880–1968) was an American deafblind author and activist whose education began with sustained support from Anne Sullivan. At a water pump in 1887, Sullivan spelled the word for water into Keller's hand while water flowed over the other, helping her connect a word with what it named. That episode was part of a much longer education. Keller graduated from Radcliffe College in 1904 and published The Story of My Life while still a student. Her writing and public advocacy continued for decades. This seven-page biographical comic follows illness, tactile language, and learning, with the later author and advocate providing context beyond the famous childhood scene.
